33179-personal-recollections-of-the-civi.creator: James Madison Stone
33179-personal-recollections-of-the-civi.description: A book by James Madison Stone. The Battle of Chantilly. CHAPTER IV WITH MCCLELLAN IN MARYLAND 83 The Barbara Fretchie Incident. The Battle of South Mountain. Death of General Reno. The Battle of Antietam. President Lincoln visits the army. Visited a farmhouse very near a Confederate Camp. CHAPTER V THE FREDERICKSBURG CAMPAIGN 101 A hard race for a pig. Chaplain Ball returns home. Picket duty along the river. The Battle of Fredericksburg. Christmas revels with the Confederates. arxiv-2105-09052.title: Methods for Detoxification of Texts for the Russian Language
arxiv-2105-09052.creator: Daryna Dementieva, Daniil Moskovskiy, Varvara Logacheva, David Dale, Olga Kozlova, Nikita Semenov, Alexander Panchenko
arxiv-2105-09052.description: Abstract We introduce the first study of automatic detoxification of Russian texts to combat offensive language. Such a kind of textual style transfer can be used, for instance, for processing toxic content in social media. While much work has been done for the English language in this field, it has never been solved for the Russian language yet.

arxiv-2203-01563.title: Emergent space-time supersymmetry at disordered quantum critical points
arxiv-2203-01563.creator: Xue-Jia Yu, Peng-Lu Zhao, Shao-Kai Jian, Zhiming Pan
arxiv-2203-01563.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xue-Jia Yu, Peng-Lu Zhao, Shao-Kai Jian, Zhiming Pan. We study the effect of disorder on the spacetime supersymmetry that is proposed to emerge at the quantum critical point of pair density wave transition in (2+1)D Dirac semimetals and (3+1)D Weyl semimetals. In the (2+1)D Dirac semimetal, we consider three types of disorder, including random scalar potential, random vector potential and random mass potential, while the random mass disorder is absent in the (3+1)D Weyl semimetal.

arxiv-2209-03224.title: Dual Instrumental Method for Confounded Kernelized Bandits
arxiv-2209-03224.creator: Xueping Gong, Jiheng Zhang
arxiv-2209-03224.description: Abstract The contextual bandit problem is a theoretically justified framework with wide applications in various fields. While the previous study on this problem usually requires independence between noise and contexts, our work considers a more sensible setting where the noise becomes a latent confounder that affects both contexts and rewards.

arxiv-2211-09489.title: How does SU( N )-natural inflation isotropize the universe?
arxiv-2211-09489.creator: Tomoaki Murata, Tomohiro Fujita, Tsutomu Kobayashi
arxiv-2211-09489.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tomoaki Murata, Tomohiro Fujita, Tsutomu Kobayashi. We study the homogeneous and anisotropic dynamics of pseudoscalar inflation coupled to an SU( N N ) gauge field. To see how the initially anisotropic universe is isotropized in such an inflation model, we derive the equations to obtain axisymmetric SU( N N ) gauge field configurations in Bianchi type-I geometry and discuss a method to identify their isotropic subsets which are the candidates of their late-time attractor.

arxiv-2304-13333.title: Neutron-proton effective mass splitting in neutron-rich matter
arxiv-2304-13333.creator: Sibo Wang, Hui Tong, Qiang Zhao, Chencan Wang, Peter Ring, Jie Meng
arxiv-2304-13333.description: Abstract Nucleon effective masses in neutron-rich matter are studied with the relativistic Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (RBHF) theory in the full Dirac space. The neutron and proton effective masses for symmetric nuclear matter are 0.80 times rest mass, which agrees well with the empirical values.

arxiv-2305-11622.title: New Garside structures and applications to Artin groups
arxiv-2305-11622.creator: Thomas Haettel and Jingyin Huang
arxiv-2305-11622.description: Abstract Abstract. Garside groups are combinatorial generalizations of braid groups which enjoy many nice algebraic, geometric, and algorithmic properties. In this article we propose a method for turning the direct product of a group G by \mathbb{Z} into a Garside group, under simple assumptions on G .

arxiv-2307-15707.title: Density-polarity coupling in confined active polar films: asters, spirals, and biphasic orientational phases
arxiv-2307-15707.creator: Mathieu Dedenon 1,2, Claire A. Dessalles 1, Pau Guillamat 3, Aurélien Roux 1, Karsten Kruse 1,2, Carles Blanch-Mercader 4
arxiv-2307-15707.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mathieu Dedenon 1,2, Claire A. Dessalles 1, Pau Guillamat 3, Aurélien Roux 1, Karsten Kruse 1,2, Carles Blanch-Mercader 4. Topological defects in active polar fluids can organise spontaneous flows and influence macroscopic density patterns. Both of them play, for example, an important role during animal development. Yet the influence of density on active flows is poorly understood.

arxiv-2406-04000.title: Stochastic logic in biased coupled photonic probabilistic bits Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2406-04000.creator: Michael Horodynski, 1,* Charles Roques-Carmes, 2,3 Yannick Salamin, 1,3 Seou Choi, 3 Jamison Sloan, 3 Di Luo, 1,4,5 and Marin Soljačić 1,3
arxiv-2406-04000.description: Abstract Optical computing often employs tailor-made hardware to implement specific algorithms, trading generality for improved performance in key aspects like speed and power efficiency. An important computing approach that is still missing its corresponding optical hardware is probabilistic computing, used e.g. for solving difficult combinatorial optimization problems.

arxiv-2409-10051.creator: Frederik Broucke
arxiv-2409-10051.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frederik Broucke. pmc-11367980.title: Endogenous electric field coupling Mxene sponge for diabetic wound management: haemostatic, antibacterial, and healing
pmc-11367980.creator: Hai Zhou, Lianglong Chen, Chaoyang Huang, Ziwei Jiang, Huihui Zhang, Xiaoyang Liu, Fengyi Zhu, Qiulan Wen, Pengwei Shi, Kun Liu, Lei Yang
pmc-11367980.description: Improper management of diabetic wound effusion and disruption of the endogenous electric field can lead to passive healing of damaged tissue, affecting the process of tissue cascade repair. This study developed an extracellular matrix sponge scaffold (K1P6@Mxene) by incorporating Mxene into an acellular dermal stroma-hydroxypropyl chitosan interpenetrating network structure.

pmc-11393644.title: Circulating dengue virus serotypes, demographics, and epidemiology in the 2023 dengue outbreak in Chittagong, Bangladesh
pmc-11393644.creator: Md. Abdur Rob, Mohabbat Hossain, M.A. Sattar, Istiaq Uddin Ahmed, Abul Faisal Md. Nuruddin Chowdhury, H.M. Hamidullah Mehedi, Noor Mohammed, Mohammed Maruf ul Quader, Md. Zakir Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman, Kallyan Chakma, Susmita Barua, Silvia Naznin Etu, Uschash Sikder, Afroza Akter Tanni, Adnan Man
pmc-11393644.description: Dengue is a serious epidemic for Bangladesh affecting thousands of lives. This study aimed to identify and determine the prevalence of the circulating variants of dengue virus (DENV) and their association with demographics and clinical manifestations among the dengue-infected patients.

pmc-11599114.title: Antiviral Peptide-Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (AVP-GPT): A Deep Learning-Powered Model for Antiviral Peptide Design with High-Throughput Discovery and Exceptional Potency
pmc-11599114.creator: Huajian Zhao, Gengshen Song
pmc-11599114.description: Traditional antiviral peptide (AVP) discovery is a time-consuming and expensive process. This study introduces AVP-GPT, a novel deep learning method utilizing transformer-based language models and multimodal architectures specifically designed for AVP design. AVP-GPT demonstrated exceptional efficiency, generating 10,000 unique peptides and identifying potential AVPs within two days on a GPU system.

pmc-11610004.title: Chronotypes in middle‐aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A population‐based study
pmc-11610004.creator: Linnea Kroneld, Päivi Polo‐Kantola, Meri‐Maija Ollila, Riikka K. Arffman, Elisa Hurskainen, Laure Morin‐Papunen, Varpu Jokimaa, Terhi T. Piltonen
pmc-11610004.description: IntroductionCircadian rhythm disruption has been associated with the risk of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), as the evening chronotype (EC) shares several traits with PCOS, including metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and psychiatric disorders. It has been suggested that the biological clock could be targeted with new, preventive, and therapeutic strategies for PCOS in women with biorhythm disorders.

pmc-12541509.title: Omics integration identified CRIP2 as a key mediator of olaparib resistance in prostate cancer
pmc-12541509.creator: Weicheng Tian, Yize Li, Haiyin Xiao, Shanghua Cai, Jinchuang Li, Biyan Wen, Zeheng Tan, Zhenjie Wu, Zhaodong Han, Yulin Deng, Yongding Wu, Huichan He, Jianheng Ye, Weide Zhong
pmc-12541509.description: BackgroundThe mechanisms driving resistance to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis), such as Olaparib, in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) that emerge after androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) remain largely undefined. This study aimed to systematically identify tumor epithelial cell subpopulations associated with Olaparib resistance by integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics (ST), and bulk RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) data, and to construct a risk prognostic model.

pmc-12581556.title: Pilot evaluation of optical genome mapping in chronic lymphocytic leukemia: complementing FISH analysis
pmc-12581556.creator: Simge Erdem, Ayşe Gül Bayrak Tokaç, Aynur Aday, Dilan Karaca, Mehmet Burak Mutlu, Kıvanç Çefle, Mustafa Nuri Yenerel, Şükrü Öztürk, Sevgi Kalayoğlu Beşışık
pmc-12581556.description: BackgroundThe clinical heterogeneity observed in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is largely attributed to diverse underlying genomic alterations. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) remains the standard cytogenetic technique but is limited to predefined loci. As a genome-wide approach, optical genome mapping (OGM) facilitates the identification of structural variants (SVs), such as copy number variations (CNVs), offering a broader genomic perspective.

pmc-12704302.title: Inhibition of immune response reduces pathology in dorsal root ganglia and peripheral nerves in cynomolgus macaques following AAV gene therapy
pmc-12704302.creator: Branka Grubor, Kate L. Henry, Su Jing Chan, Mark Sheehan, Anumeha Shah, Alex Pellerin, Judy Bai, Prasad Nadella, Santhosh Bommegowda, Patrick Cullen, Eric Tien, Vivian Chen, Nicholas P. van der Munnik, Stephanie White-Hunt, Edward D. Plowey, Stefan Hamann, Amanda J. Guise, Shanqin Xu, Melissa Kirkla
pmc-12704302.description: Administration of adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapies via blood or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in non-human primates (NHPs) can lead to degeneration of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons and nerve fibers in the spinal cord and peripheral nerves. AAV cargo expression is implicated in AAV DRG toxicity, but the underlying mechanism(s) is unknown.

pmc-13285677.title: Updating “A nationally representative dataset of 1549 Americans aged 18 to 94 on interest in, experience with, and barriers to cogeneration, defined as working with older and younger people for social good” with data on religious identity and service attendance
pmc-13285677.creator: Cal J Halvorsen, Andrew Joung, Stefanie Weiss, Jacob Stolmeier

pmc-13295737.title: A Novel Monoclonal Antibody Targeting the A29 Protein of Monkeypox Virus and Its Application in Immunoassay
pmc-13295737.creator: Nan Jia, Weixiao Wang, Guangwei Zhao, Danfei Meng, Liyuan Zheng, Jinhua Dong
pmc-13295737.description: Background: The monkeypox virus (MPXV) has attracted considerable global attention due to its potential to cause widespread outbreaks, necessitating the development of rapid and accurate diagnostic methods of significant clinical importance. A29, a key envelope protein of MPXV, represents a promising diagnostic target.

pmc-13454354.title: Randomized phase 2 trial of a PARP inhibitor TSL-1502 in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer
pmc-13454354.creator: Bo Lan, Faliang Xu, Tao Sun, Fuming Qiu, Yongsheng Wang, Shouman Wang, Wei Li, Yahua Zhong, Xinhong Wu, Quchang Ouyang, Ke Wang, Xiaolan Mi, Rui Liu, Binghe Xu
pmc-13454354.description: Glucuronide prodrug strategies may enhance target specificity and reduce the toxicity of PARP inhibitors, but no clinical evaluation has been performed. We evaluated TSL-1502, a novel glucuronide prodrug of a PARP inhibitor, in a randomized, open-label, phase 2 study at 28 sites in China (NCT05420779).

pmc-13544187.title: CAR T-cell therapy as a definitive consolidation for older adults with B-ALL in first complete remission∗†
pmc-13544187.creator: Ibrahim Aldoss, Lior Goldberg, Jianying Zhang, Andrew Artz, Mary C Clark, Min Guan, Ruby Espinosa, Thiruvaimozhi Abimannan, Jiaqi Wu, Bryan Garcia, Eric R Haas, Khyatiben V Pathak, Brooke Lovell, Patrick Pirrotte, Vaibhav Agrawal, Neguine Sanani, Stephanie Kasten, Dileshni Tilakawardane, Jamie R Wag
pmc-13544187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key Points•First-line CAR T-cell therapy for adults with ALL in CR was safe and tolerable and potentially extended the duration of remission.•Clinical samples of patients in remission and patients with relapsed ALL had distinct inflammatory and immunometabolic profiles.

pmc-13658020.title: The Geopolitics of Expert Knowledge: Analysing the European Commission’s Role and Influence in Indonesian Higher Education
pmc-13658020.creator: Sotiria Grek, Hilary MacDonogh
pmc-13658020.description: Building on a rich set of policy documents and interview data, and using the concept of the epistemic infrastructure, the article focuses on an analysis of how European HE expert actors became the preferred advisers for Indonesia’s HE quality assurance system.
